entries.title: The Currently log
entries.summary: Every change of Petto is posted in this channel when it goes live: a color for each kind of change, a short explanation, and pictures. React with the like or the dislike to tell us what you think. Red is security, yellow a new feature, green something added to a feature, blue an improvement, orange a fix, purple the web and docs, gray something removed and black a feature removed.

entries.title: Top lists of the best partner managers
entries.summary: `{partner.top_list_day}`, `{partner.top_list_week}` and `{partner.top_list_total}` write the five best managers of the day, the week and all time, one per line with their partnerships. Use them in any partner message.

entries.title: 14 new server and member variables
entries.summary: Server: `{server_age_days}`, `{server_createdate_timestamp}`, `{server_emojicount}`, `{server_stickercount}`, `{server_description}`, `{server_vanity}`, `{server_banner}`, `{server_verification}`, `{server_locale}` and `{server_rules_channel}`. Member: `{user.role_count}`, `{user.top_role_mention}`, `{user.is_owner}` and `{user.joined_age_days}`.

entries.title: Purge in every channel
entries.summary: `/purge` and `!purge` have a new option, `all_channels` (or `!purge everywhere 50 bots`). It scans every text channel where you and Petto can delete, shows how many messages it would delete in each one, and waits for a Confirm click before deleting anything.

entries.title: New command: /mhistory
entries.summary: `/mhistory moderator:<member>` and `!mhistory <moderator>` show the cases a moderator has given. The line of `/case stats` that pointed to it now names a command that exists.

entries.title: A case shows the same icon everywhere
entries.summary: The card of a case (`/case view`, `/case edit`) and the one-line case still used the old icon of each sanction type. They now use the hammer, or the alert for a warning, like the list of cases.

entries.title: /forum outside a post says why
entries.summary: Using `/forum` in a channel that is not a forum post answered with a generic error. It now tells you to use it inside a post.

entries.title: /guildtag and /vanity show in the menu
entries.summary: Discord hid both commands from members without Manage Server, so a moderator could not find them. They now show for everybody and ask for Manage Server when they run.

entries.title: !c opens the cases
entries.summary: `!c <member>` is now a short way of `!case`: it shows the cases of that member.

entries.title: !c is no longer the calculator
entries.summary: `c` was a short word of the calculator, so `!c <id>` answered with a calculation. `!calc` and `!calculate` still work.

entries.title: New blog post: Introducing the Currently log
entries.summary: What the Currently log is, what each color means, how a post looks and what is in the first one. Available in English, Spanish and Portuguese.

entries.title: A sticky message is posted when you save it
entries.summary: Saving a sticky message in the dashboard now posts it in the channel right away, like `!stickymessage set` does, instead of waiting for somebody to write there first. If you change it, the old message is replaced.

entries.title: Text fields fit their text
entries.summary: Every text field of the site has the height of its text: no corner to drag, it grows as you write and shrinks as you delete, and an empty one is four lines high. Chat boxes keep their own size.

entries.title: The "New" label goes away by itself
entries.summary: The "New" label on the tabs of the dashboard, the modules, the menu and the footer now lasts ten days from the day something comes out. The ones that were still showing it after weeks are gone.

entries.title: Sticky messages come back down for bots too
entries.summary: A sticky message used to ignore what bots wrote, so in a channel where bots do the talking it stayed far above. Now a message from anybody (members, bots and webhooks) brings it back to the bottom.

entries.title: A ban with deleted messages answers first
entries.summary: When you ban someone and ask to delete their recent messages, Petto now sends the notice, bans, says it is done and writes the log first, and deletes the messages after. Before, a member with many messages made you wait for the deletion before seeing the answer.

entries.title: Purge in every channel also cleans threads and forum posts
entries.summary: `/purge all_channels` skipped threads and the posts of forums, so what was written there stayed. It now scans the open ones too, and they appear in the confirmation list. An archived thread is left alone: nothing can be deleted there until it is opened again.

entries.title: Ticket transcripts show forwarded messages
entries.summary: A forwarded message used to appear in the transcript as "No text content", because the text lives in the original message. Now the transcript shows what was forwarded (its text, embeds, files and stickers) under a "Forwarded" mark, and the live view of the ticket shows it too.

entries.title: Petto Code can now manage the server
entries.summary: Commands written in code can now edit, delete and pin messages, read messages, users and permissions, and run a command later. From a button, a menu, a form or a reaction they can also moderate (warn, mute, kick, ban), lock channels and manage roles, threads and nicknames, always with the permissions of the member who pressed it: a typed command cannot copy what Petto already does with its own commands. There are also 30 small tools for text, numbers, lists and dates.

entries.title: Petto Code: files, connected commands and reminders that repeat
entries.summary: A command can now be written in several files: the + above the editor adds one (up to 5), and they run together as one code. A command can use another one (callCC) and give a value back, run a command of Petto as the member (runCommand), and run by itself every some time, every day or every week in a time zone. One panel under the editor sets what starts it, the commands that run after it, who can use it and where (roles and channels), what a mistake does, and the server time zone. The editor is also bigger on a phone.

entries.title: Roles and channels are easier to pick in the dashboard
entries.area: Dashboard › Lists of roles and channels
entries.summary: Every list of roles and channels in the dashboard now has a box to tick in each row. Roles show their color, channels sit under their category like in Discord, and a role that Petto cannot give (above Petto, or managed) shows dark and locked with the reason. A list that only filters keeps those roles, with a small mark. On a phone the same compact menu opens, and tapping a text field closes an open list, so what you type goes to that field.

entries.title: Roles in their own color, categories with their emoji
entries.area: Dashboard › Lists of roles and channels
entries.summary: In every list of the dashboard a role is now written in its own color, as Discord shows it, and in the chip that stays when it is chosen. A category whose name starts with an emoji shows that emoji first in its title, in the lists and in the compact menu. Tapping a text field while a list is open now puts the phone's keyboard in that field, never in the list, and the file tabs of the code editor meet the code box with one soft outline.

entries.title: One Save button for the whole Code page
entries.summary: Change the options of a command, the time zone, the connected commands, the trigger or the code, and the bar at the bottom says "You have unsaved changes" with Discard and Save changes for all of it together. Save sends every change, one after the other; Discard puts everything back as it was.

entries.title: A little ring turns inside a switch while it saves
entries.summary: Every switch of the dashboard is the same green, and while a change is being saved a small ring turns inside its knob, like the ones of the quick access in the overview. The page does not reload, so it feels smoother.

entries.title: Green to save and choose, red to delete
entries.summary: In the dashboard, the buttons that save or add are green, the ones that delete are red, and what you have chosen (options, chips, tabs and ticks) is green too. The peach stays for the menu and the links.

entries.title: The log of a sanction that ends shows who it was
entries.summary: When a timed mute or ban ends by itself, the log now shows the name, the ID and the avatar of the person at the top, like the log of a new sanction. Before, it only had the ID.

entries.title: `!level roles` shows the roles of the levels
entries.summary: `!level roles` (and `!level rewards`) is the same as `!level reward list` and `/level reward list`: the roles you get at each level. Before, it said it could not find `roles`.

entries.title: The color card says why it has no picture
entries.summary: `/search color`, `!color` and `!hex` draw a picture of the color. Where Petto or the member cannot attach files in the channel, the picture was left out without a word; now the card says why, so you know to give Petto the Attach Files permission.

entries.title: A bulk role job no longer stops with an error when the server is just back
entries.summary: If the roles of the server were not loaded yet (the server had just come back, or Discord was slow), a bulk role job stopped with an unexpected error. Now Petto loads the roles first, and if it still cannot read them it says so and you can start the job again.

entries.title: Petto's libraries are up to date
entries.summary: Four of the libraries Petto uses were updated to their latest versions (images, settings, the request limit and the payments kit). Nothing changes for you, but it keeps Petto safe and ready for what comes.

entries.title: The Petto Code wiki has a step by step guide, recipes and a full reference
entries.summary: The Petto Code wiki is much longer: a guide that goes step by step, ten recipes you can copy (a welcome, a shop, a reminder...), and a reference of every function with an example. On a phone, the tables are cards, so a long name is never cut in the middle.

entries.title: Tables of the wiki are cards on a phone
entries.summary: On a phone, each row of a table of the wiki (like the variables) is a card, so a long variable is never cut in the middle and you do not have to scroll sideways.

entries.title: The Code Generator knows every function of Petto Code
entries.summary: The Code Generator (version 1.7.0) runs the same engine as the bot again: all the new functions of Petto Code, connected commands, repeating reminders, and the mistakes it finds are written in the language of the page.

entries.title: A change reaches the Currently log in two minutes
entries.summary: Petto now looks for new changes every two minutes, not every ten, so what is merged and deployed shows in this channel almost at once instead of looking like it was forgotten.

entries.title: The pictures of a change are checked before it is posted
entries.summary: Petto now reads each picture of a change the way Discord does (it has to be a real image of a size Discord takes) and leaves it ready, so one of the three pictures of a change no longer shows broken. A change whose picture does not pass waits until it does.

entries.title: The Improvements card has an arrow that goes up
entries.summary: The card of the improvements had two circular arrows that looked like a clock. It now has an arrow that goes up.

entries.title: Petto uses less memory
entries.summary: Petto used a lot of memory keeping every message it saw for an hour, even in servers that do not use the message log. Now it keeps them for ten minutes, and for an hour only in the servers that have the message log on, so the log of edited and deleted messages works as before. A lighter Petto stays fast as it grows.

entries.title: The statistics overview shows voice next to messages
entries.summary: The overview of the statistics now draws the voice hours per day and the busiest hours of voice right next to the messages per day and the busiest hours of messages, so you see both at a glance. The Voice tab keeps its own details.

entries.title: Petto no longer works for logs a server did not turn on
entries.summary: Before building a log, Petto now checks that the server has that log on. A server without the voice log or the message log no longer makes Petto ask Discord who muted, moved or disconnected someone, or build the embed for every edit and deletion. Servers with the logs on get them exactly as before.

entries.title: /stats member now comes as two picture cards
entries.summary: /stats member shows a profile card with the member's server rank for messages and voice, when the account was created and when they joined, and their messages and voice time in the last day, 7 days and 30 days. Under it, a second card has the streak, active days, best day and a chart of messages and voice hours per day. Voice time counts now, not only messages. Every /stats picture now shows the icon of your server next to its name. The pictures here show the main Petto server with made-up numbers.

entries.title: A channel Petto cannot see is no longer called deleted
entries.summary: Discord now shows the channels a bot cannot view only in outline. The dashboard used to call a saved choice that pointed to one of them (a log, a feed, a honeypot or a paginated list) a deleted channel. It now says No access (hidden channel), because the channel exists and Petto just cannot see it. The channel pickers still do not list those channels.

entries.title: Tickets answered by AI are removed
entries.summary: The AI assistant for tickets is gone, for good. Its answers were not reliable enough and it used more resources than it was worth. Petto no longer greets or answers in new tickets with the AI, the Talk to a person button and the AI assistant page of the dashboard are removed, and so are its settings in the server's YAML. Staff answer tickets as always. The /ask command stays.

entries.title: Privacy Policy and Terms explain /ask and follow Canadian law
entries.summary: The Privacy Policy and the Terms now explain how /ask works: only the question, and up to four earlier messages of a conversation, go to the AI provider; Petto stores none of it and does not use it to train AI; the provider may process it outside Canada. Petto follows the principles of Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA, and Law 25 in Québec) and names Liam as the person responsible for privacy. The Terms are governed by the laws of Colombia. The old texts about the ticket assistant are gone.

entries.title: /language and /support are slash commands
entries.summary: /language, to see or change the language Petto speaks on your server, and the new /support, which gives you the invitation to the support server, now work as slash commands. The prefix commands !language and !support keep working too.

entries.title: The welcome message of a new server uses slash commands
entries.summary: When Petto joins a server, the setup message and the guide for the owner now point to /help, /logs, /automod, /greet and /language instead of the prefix commands, and the invitation to the support server is in it. The picture next to the text is the avatar Petto has in that server, so a Christmas avatar shows up too, and every line has its icon.

entries.title: The dashboard login asks if you want to join the support server
entries.summary: The first time you sign in to the dashboard, a question asks whether you want Petto to add you to the support server, with Yes and No. Only if you say yes does Discord ask you to allow it on its own screen. It is asked once, and nobody is added without saying yes.

entries.title: The wiki publishes again and the Priority changelog is up to date
entries.summary: The wiki had stopped publishing its latest changes because of an error in a file meant for the team. It is fixed, so what was written about /ask and privacy is online. The Priority changelog now shows the news of 2026-11-18 and its text no longer sits in a narrow column under the date. The Language and Statistics pages describe /language and the new /stats member pictures.

entries.title: What Petto stored for a server is deleted 5 minutes after it is removed
entries.summary: When Petto is removed from a server, everything it stored for that server is deleted at most 5 minutes later, not after 3 days: the settings, the logs and the backups kept in its database, with no exceptions (a Premium slot in use or backups no longer make it wait). If the bot is added back inside those minutes, nothing is lost. The servers that were waiting for their 3 days are deleted now. The Privacy Policy says so in English, Spanish and Portuguese.

entries.title: Quick Setup: set up your server in seven steps from the dashboard
entries.summary: A new guided setup in the dashboard menu. Pick the modules you want (moderation log, auto moderation, welcome messages, auto role, tickets, verification), answer a few questions in each step and nothing changes in your server until the last step, when everything is applied together. Petto can make the channels and roles for you, and a step that fails does not stop the others. You can run it again any time from the sidebar.

entries.title: Moderation rules: make your own rules in the dashboard
entries.summary: A new, much more powerful way to moderate. Make rulesets with general conditions (channels, categories, roles, new accounts) and rules inside them: choose what to look for (words, links with allow and deny lists, invites, mentions, caps, emojis, repeated or too fast messages, attachments and more), who and where it applies, and what Petto does (delete, reply, DM, warn, timeout, kick, ban, give or take a role), even only after a member does it several times. There is a log of what each rule did, without the text of messages. Rules are made only in the dashboard.

entries.title: Every page of the dashboard now ends with what happens to your data
entries.summary: At the bottom of every server page there is now a short note: Petto keeps your settings while it is in your server, deletes them within 5 minutes if you remove it, and where to make a backup, export your settings, read the docs, get support or read the Privacy Policy.
